extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and analyzing athletic contests (college and professional football/baseball) for a newspaper audience, including play-by-play description, box scores, and postgame analysis of tactics and individual performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team spirit and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: “Through sheer spirit, through indomitable determination, through utter willingness to give the final measure of physical sacrifice…” (used to explain Yale's victory over Princeton).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize intangible qualities — grit, refusal to yield — as decisive factors that can overcome a technically superior opponent; use narrative language to show how spirit influenced the result (examples: Yale's sustained effort, crowd reaction, players not yielding until carried from the field).

rubrics_metrics.name: All-around team work / cohesion
rubrics_metrics.description: “In all-around team work Yale outshone Princeton.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how well players perform collectively (following the ball, supporting ball-carriers, consistent tackling) rather than just individual flashes; cite examples of coordinated plays and collective defense or offense when explaining superiority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offensive strategy and variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast between “wide open attack” (backfield passing and runs around the end) and “close formation and concealed ball offense.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the offense uses a varied, adaptable approach (sweeps, end runs, forward passes) or relies on a single formation; note how variety can bewilder defenses and produce scoring opportunities, with examples of successful wide-open attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punting and kicking duels / field-position management
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics and commentary on punt exchanges: “Yale punted 27 times to Princeton's 40 and showed an average gain of close to four yards in each exchange of punts.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use punting frequency, punt distance/returns, and who 'outdistanced' whom to judge territorial advantage; show how superior punts set up scoring chances or relieve defensive pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward passing effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit pass statistics: “Yale essayed seven forward passes ... gaining 69 yards to Princeton's 0.” Also narrative notes on poor throws, drops, and blocked/grounded passes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure passing by attempts, yards gained, completions, and impact plays; discuss throw quality (spiral, accuracy), receiver catches or drops, and how passing affected defensive alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rushing yardage and first downs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of rushing totals and first downs as evidence: “Yale gained 298 yards by rushing ... and made 15 first downs to the Tigers' 11.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report yardage totals and first-down counts to quantify dominance or parity; use them to explain control of the game and ability to sustain drives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties and their effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalty yardage and frequency: “Penalties were numerous ... Yale losing 80 yards in eight setbacks to Princeton's 60 in seven infringements.” Also penalization for undue roughness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List number and yardage of penalties and describe particular infractions that shifted momentum or led directly to scores; call out rough or unsportsmanlike acts and official enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fumbles, drops and turnovers
rubrics_metrics.description: Game-turning errors such as fumbles and dropped catches (e.g., Moore's catch that glanced from his fingers, fumbles that cost scoring chances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight ball-handling mistakes and recoveries; show how turnovers altered field position or scoring opportunities; use specific instances (dropped lateral, fumble on punt return) to explain result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutions, depth and late-game impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting how second/third-string players changed the dynamic: when Yale sent in substitutes the Tigers made progress; “Including the original line-up, substitutions and re-substitutions, 57 players took part in the game.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate bench strength and how substitutions affected momentum in later quarters; report which subs contributed and whether starters were rested or reinserted at key moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coaching, generalship and playcalling
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit criticism/praise of coaches: “Click's generalship was execrable... turning time and again to centre plunges, usually unsuccessfully.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess tactical decisions (choice of plays, when to kick, going for field goals vs. touchdowns); point out obvious mismatches between playcalling and opponent weaknesses as evidence of poor generalship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual performance and role-specific skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of standout players and their contributions (e.g., Le Gore, Scovil, Guernsey, Gapt Ballin, E. Trenkmann).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe players' key skills — punting, passing, tackling, end runs, line plunging — and use examples (long runs, interceptions, blocking) to justify 'star' status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special teams/kicking (drop-kicks/field goals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of kickers and drop-kicking: Guernsey's toe artistry and Cuemsey's fifty-three-yard field goal are singled out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report kicking attempts and successes, note long/remarkable kicks, and explain how a reliable toe can remove need for touchdowns; include rules context when a kick was nullified by a penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive fundamentals (tackling, following the ball, formations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific defensive traits: “following the ball and in holding it,” “wing defence,” “defence off tackle,” and criticism of normal defensive arrangement “three abreast, twelve yards back, is open to grave criticism.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze defensive alignment, tackling consistency, and ability to pursue and hold ball-carriers; point out tactical vulnerabilities and suggest areas for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation suitability relative to situation
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentary on formation fit: “Her forward-passing game is not dangerous, and she launches a driving attack from her Minnesota shift formation better qualified for midfield gains than for gains inside her opponent's thirty-five-yard line.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether a chosen formation suits the team's goals and opponent's weaknesses; explain trade-offs (midfield control vs. red-zone effectiveness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of statistics and box scores to support narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of detailed box scores, line-ups, inning-by-inning and play statistics for baseball and full stat lines for football (yards, punts, penalties, fumbles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement color reporting with concrete stats (yards, hits, errors, innings, box scores) to back interpretive claims; provide line-ups and official scorers/umpires for completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid narrative / anecdotal description
rubrics_metrics.description: Colorful, scene-setting prose and anecdotes (e.g., long account of Ty Cobb's daring baserunning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid verbs, simile, and moment-by-moment description to recreate key plays and personalities; balance this with factual accuracy and clear identification of players.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field and weather context, attendance and crowd effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting conditions: “The day was dark and cloudy ... light sprinkling of rain ... strong, cold wind,” and attendance anecdotes like Rockland Day delegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mention weather, field conditions, crowd size and special delegations if they influenced play or atmosphere; use crowd reaction to illustrate emotional stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officials, rulings and procedural enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials' actions affected outcomes (e.g., referee set Princeton back fifteen yards for Brown speaking to Capt. Click; umpire awarding/denying plays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document key officiating decisions, penalties assessed for conduct, and any controversies; explain rule application where it materially changed scoring or field position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseball pitching evaluation (control, endurance, effectiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments such as “Cheney was wild and ineffective,” “Tesreau ... was very wild, but the Chicago batsmen could not hit him with men on bases,” and praise for Ernie Shore 'settling down.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate pitchers on command (walks), hits allowed, strikeouts, ability to settle after shaky innings, and situational effectiveness; cite inning-by-inning performance and relief appearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseball fielding and throwing precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Fielding plays and throwing accuracy (e.g., five bases stolen on Archer, two passed balls; Cady's throws to second that prevented advancement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight defensive plays that saved runs or erased threats; quantify passed balls, errors, and assists where relevant and describe miscues that led to runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base running aggression and craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of daring baserunning and steals (Ty Cobb's aggressive steals and runs), and their psychological effect on opponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report steals, heads-up base running decisions, and how aggressiveness pressured defenses or shifted momentum; dramatize with play detail but retain accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactical substitutions and pinch-hitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of pinch hitters and late substitutions in baseball (e.g., Dubuc sent in to bat for Coveleskie), and strategic re-insertion of varsity players in football.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the timing and results of managerial substitutions and pinch hitters; assess whether they changed the game's outcome or were merely marginal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training regimen and preparation (collegiate crews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic advice: “Daily work on the machines will then be ordered, and the crew men will not have any further let-up in their training.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When previewing team prospects, report planned training schedules, coach directives, and expected continuity of practice as indicators of future performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sportsmanship and conduct criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial remarks about rough play leaving “a bad taste in the mouth,” even when no injury resulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out conduct that violates the spirit of play even if within the rules, discuss its effect on spectators and reputation, and report penalties or rebukes from officials.
